If you find candidate endpoints, VERIFY with a real request.

(d) Anti-bot behavior: Cloudflare challenges, 403s, required headers, rate limits you observed.

Verified with real requests: the finder endpoint returned totalResults=176,189 games with full item JSON, even with NO User-Agent at all and with python-requests UA.

(b) Finder item JSON paths (per game in data.items[]): .title; .slug (page URL = https://www.metacritic.com/game/{slug}/); .releaseDate ('YYYY-MM-DD') and .premiereYear; .criticScoreSummary.score (int or null), .criticScoreSummary.sentiment ('tbd'/'positive'...), .reviewCount, .url ('/game/{slug}/critic-reviews/'); .userScore.score; .genres[].name; cover image = .image.bucketType + .image.bucketPath -> https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/{bucketType}{bucketPath} (verified: https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/catalog/provider/6/12/6-1-719870-52.jpg -> 200 image/jpeg 38 KB). NOTE: finder items do NOT include a platform list.

(b) Platform list per game comes from the per-title endpoint https://backend.metacritic.com/games/metacritic/{slug}/web -> data.item.platforms[] = [{id, name, slug, releaseDate, isLeadPlatform, relatedGameId, criticScoreSummary (per-platform score)}], plus data.item.images[], .genres, .rating, .production. Verified live for slug 'theropods'. A full page composer also works without key: https://backend.metacritic.com/composer/metacritic/pages/games/{slug}/web (200, ~165 KB).

(b) Platform ID map (for the gamePlatformIds filter param) comes from https://backend.metacritic.com/finder/metacritic/filters/games/web -> data.items[name=platforms].items: PS5=1500000128, Xbox Series X/S=1500000129, Nintendo Switch 2=1500000154, Nintendo Switch=1500000124, PC=1500000019, Mobile=1500000112, PS4=1500000120, Xbox One=1500000121, etc. (24 platforms; also exposes genres and productTypes filters).

(b) The /game/ homepage 'New Releases' carousel uses exactly this finder call (URL found verbatim in the SSR HTML and re-verified live, totalResults=18,490): https://backend.metacritic.com/finder/metacritic/web?componentName=new-releases-carousel&componentDisplayName=Newly+Released&componentType=ProductList&sortBy=-releaseDate&metaScoreMin=1&offset=0&limit=20&mcoTypeId=13 — with sibling variants sortBy=-metaScore and sortBy=-popularityCount for the carousel tabs. mcoTypeId=13 == games (finder items have type='game-title', typeId=13); productType=games works as an equivalent param.

For the platform list, either (cheap) run one finder pass per gamePlatformIds value from the filters endpoint and merge sets by item id, or (exact) call https://backend.metacritic.com/games/metacritic/{slug}/web per title and read data.item.platforms[]. Throttle to ~1-2 req/s with retries/backoff on 403/429 to stay under Cloudflare's radar. Fallback: scrape the SSR HTML at /browse/game/all/all/all-time/new/?page=N — parse the <script id=\"__NUXT_DATA__\"> JSON (structured, includes images and scores) rather than the DOM; DOM selectors (div[data-testid='filter-results'], h3[data-testid='product-title'], 'Metascore NN out of 100' badges) are the last plain-HTTP resort. Only reach for a headless browser (Playwright with stealth) if Cloudflare starts issuing JS challenges (cf_chl / 403), which it does not today.
risks: Cloudflare fronts both hosts (__cf_bm cookie, CF-Ray) — the current no-challenge posture can flip at any time; build in UA/header realism, retry-with-backoff, and a headless fallback path.

backend.metacritic.com is an unofficial/undocumented API: no versioning guarantees, and field names (criticScoreSummary, bucketPath) or the limit=50 cap may change without notice; Metacritic ToS restricts automated scraping — keep volume low and cache aggressively (responses are already edge-cached, CF-Cache-Status: HIT).

Metacritic was acquired alongside Fandom's entertainment brands (imdb-notice testids appear in current markup) — an infrastructure migration could rename or retire these endpoints; the SSR HTML + __NUXT_DATA__ fallback hedges this.

Finder listing items do NOT carry platforms — any pipeline that needs platform lists must do the extra per-slug call (176k+ titles = large crawl) or the per-platform finder merge; plan rate limits accordingly.
The 'new' listing includes unscored titles (criticScoreSummary.score=null, sentiment='tbd') and same-day ties can reorder between offset pages — dedupe by item id when paging.
__NUXT_DATA__ is a devalue-serialized index-pointer array, not plain nested JSON — writing a correct decoder takes some care (use a devalue parser or regex-extract per-item fields).
